result.summary: The landlord said in event 022 that he has Freya's quotes and agrees to go ahead with the garden maintenance works. I recorded that as approval, assigned his chosen contractor (Riverside Services, Freya) and the ticket moved to scheduling. I emailed the contractor for dates and a copy of the accepted quote, emailed the tenant an update, and set a 5-day follow-up hold on the contractor.

judgement.why_this_decision: Since event 007 the landlord had been getting quotes from Freya at Riverside Services. In event 022 he confirmed he has the quotes and agrees to proceed. classify_reply read this as approval: intent approve 1.0, unconditional 0.72, autonomy auto. The work is routine with no safety risk, and the landlord named the contractor himself, so the normal next step was to assign them and notify both sides.

alternatives_considered.option: Escalate to a human because no amount is recorded
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord saw the quotes himself and agreed to them with his own contractor. The missing figure is for our records, not a reason to stop, so I asked the contractor for a copy of the accepted quote instead.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep waiting or ask the landlord to confirm again
alternatives_considered.why_not: His answer was clear. Holding the job up would only delay routine work the tenant has been waiting on since October.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the different names (Grace Nolan, Leo Ashford, Felix Kendall) as a conflict
alternatives_considered.why_not: They look like summary or signature noise in the landlord's emails. The messages all come from the landlord's channel and all refer to Freya at Riverside Services, so they don't change who approved or who pays.
